_meta.source: Compiled from ASNT SNT-TC-1A (2024 ed.), ASME BPVC Section V (2023), AWS D1.1 (2020), API 510/570/653 (current eds.), ISO 9712:2021. Day-rate ranges reflect mid-2025 US market data from ASNT salary survey + industry contractor schedules; international rates approximate.

UT.name: Ultrasonic Testing
UT.principle: High-frequency sound waves (0.5-20 MHz) transmitted through material reflect from internal discontinuities or back-walls; transit time and amplitude reveal flaw depth and size.
typicalUseCases: Weld inspection (full penetration butt welds, fillet welds)
Wall-thickness corrosion mapping on piping and pressure vessels
Lamination detection in plate and pipe
Bond testing in composites and bonded structures

calibrationRequirements.frequency: Daily verification at start of shift; full calibration min. annually per ASNT recommended
calibrationRequirements.asmeRef: ASME BPVC Section V Article 4 — sensitivity per T-462
calibrationRequirements.linearityChecks: Vertical/horizontal linearity per Article 4 Mandatory Appendix I; amplitude control linearity ±20%
calibrationRequirements.tempCorrection: Velocity correction needed if material/wedge differ >25°F from cal-block temperature

prerequisiteCertifications: Vision: near 20/30 each eye, color contrast (Ishihara)
ASNT SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410 employer-written practice
limitationsAndCaveats: Difficult on coarse-grain austenitic stainless and Inconel welds
Surface finish must be Ra <12.5 µm typically
complementaryMethods: MT/PT (for surface flaws missed by UT)

RT.name: Radiographic Testing
RT.principle: Penetrating ionising radiation (X-rays from generator OR gamma rays from Ir-192/Co-60/Se-75 isotope) attenuates differentially through material; film or digital detector captures latent image showing density variations from internal discontinuities.
typicalUseCases: Butt-weld inspection on pipe and plate
Casting porosity, shrinkage, and inclusion detection
Pipeline construction (girth weld qualification per API 1104)
Field RT on refinery and petchem turnarounds

iridiumSourcePriceUSD.note: Ir-192 ~75-day half-life — new source every 90 days typical

calibrationRequirements.frequency: Source-strength decay calculated at every exposure; survey meter cal annual; densitometer cal monthly + at use
calibrationRequirements.iqi: Hole-type or wire IQI per ASTM E1025/E747; sensitivity 2-2T typically
calibrationRequirements.geometricUnsharpness: Ug < 0.020 in. for materials <2 in.; calculated from source size, OFD, FFD

limitationsAndCaveats: Radiation hazard — exclusion zones up to 200+ ft
Tight cracks parallel to film plane often missed
Material thickness limits (Ir-192 max ~2.5 in. steel)
Slow vs. UT for thickness mapping

MT.name: Magnetic Particle Testing
MT.fullName: Magnetic Particle Inspection (Wet Fluorescent / Dry Visible)
MT.principle: Ferromagnetic component is magnetised; surface or near-surface discontinuities create flux leakage that attracts iron-oxide particles (dry powder, wet bath, or fluorescent suspension), revealing crack-like indications.
typicalUseCases: Forging and casting surface flaw detection
In-service crack detection on cranes, drilling rigs, structural steel

calibrationRequirements.frequency: Yoke lift test daily (10 lb AC, 40 lb DC per ASTM E709); UV lamp 1000+ µW/cm² at 15 in.; particle bath concentration twice per shift via centrifuge tube
calibrationRequirements.ketosRing: Pie-gauge or QQI shim verification at start of shift
calibrationRequirements.asmeRef: ASME BPVC Section V Article 7 / Article 25 SE-709
calibrationRequirements.ambientLightMax: <2 fc (20 lux) for fluorescent; >100 fc for visible

prerequisiteCertifications: Vision: near 20/30, color (Ishihara) for visible particles
limitationsAndCaveats: Ferromagnetic only (no austenitic stainless, aluminium, copper)

PT.name: Liquid Penetrant Testing
PT.principle: Low-viscosity dye is applied to clean surface; capillary action draws penetrant into surface-breaking discontinuities; excess removed; developer pulls penetrant back to surface revealing flaw outline (visible red-on-white or fluorescent under UV-A).
typicalUseCases: Casting surface porosity and crack detection

calibrationRequirements.frequency: Per-shift system performance check on TAM/PSM panel; UV-A intensity ≥1000 µW/cm² at 15 in.; ambient white light <2 fc for fluorescent
calibrationRequirements.dwellTime: Penetrant 5-30 min per material/temp; developer 7-30 min minimum
calibrationRequirements.tempRange: 40-125°F standard; outside range requires qualification per ASTM E1417

limitationsAndCaveats: Surface prep critical — no oils, paint, scale
Slower than MT on ferromagnetic parts

ET.name: Eddy Current Testing
ET.fullName: Electromagnetic / Eddy Current Testing (Single-Frequency, Multi-Frequency, Eddy Current Array)
ET.principle: Alternating current in a probe coil induces eddy currents in conductive material; surface or near-surface flaws disrupt eddy-current flow, producing measurable impedance change displayed on impedance plane.
typicalUseCases: Surface crack detection through thin coatings
Aircraft structural inspection (wing skins, lap joints)

calibrationRequirements.frequency: Reference standard with known EDM notches verified at start of every job; freq./gain noted per inspection
referenceStandards: ASME E215 EDM notch sets (0.005, 0.010, 0.020 in.)
ASTM E243 reference tubes for HX work
calibrationRequirements.asmeRef: ASME BPVC Section V Article 8 (ET) / Article 26 SE-243
calibrationRequirements.frequencyRange: 100 Hz to 10 MHz typical; HX tubing 5-400 kHz
calibrationRequirements.fillFactor: Bobbin probe fill factor >0.85 for HX tubes

prerequisiteCertifications: Employer practice per SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410
outputArtifacts: Indication call list w/ tube map
limitationsAndCaveats: Limited depth of penetration (~3 mm in steel at 100 kHz)
Lift-off and edge effects require operator skill

VT.name: Visual Testing
VT.principle: Direct or aided visual examination of accessible surfaces using natural or artificial light, optionally augmented by mirrors, borescopes, videoscopes, magnifiers, or remote cameras; the foundational NDT method preceding all others.
typicalUseCases: Borescope inspection of turbine blades, vessel internals, HX shell-side
Pre-test prep verification for all other NDT methods

videoscopeUSD.models: Olympus IPLEX, Karl Storz Techno Pack

calibrationRequirements.frequency: Light meter cal annual; weld gauges visual verification per use; borescope optical cal annual
calibrationRequirements.lightingMin: 100 fc (1000 lux) at examination surface per ASME V Art. 9
calibrationRequirements.remoteVTResolution: Discriminate 1/32 in. wire at max examination distance per Article 9

prerequisiteCertifications: Vision: Jaeger J2 (or equiv) at 12 in.
complementaryMethods: Performed before every other NDT method

PAUT.name: Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing
PAUT.fullName: Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing (Linear, Sectorial, Compound, Matrix)
PAUT.principle: Multi-element transducer (16-256 piezo elements) fired with controlled time delays steers and focuses ultrasonic beam electronically; produces sectorial (S-scan), linear (L-scan), and compound images of weld volume in real time.
typicalUseCases: Code-replacement for RT on heavy-wall pipe and pressure vessel welds (per ASME Code Case 2235)
Pipeline AUT on cross-country construction (per API 1104 Annex)
Corrosion mapping on vessels and tank floors

instrument16x16USD.models: Olympus OmniScan MX2, Eddyfi M2M Gekko

calibrationRequirements.frequency: Wedge delay + element check at every job; sensitivity cal on weld-specific block
blocks: Custom weld-mockup block w/ EDM notches matching weld profile + thickness
calibrationRequirements.asmeRef: ASME BPVC Section V Article 4 + Mandatory Appendix IV (PAUT)
calibrationRequirements.elementHealth: Active element check at start of shift; <25% dead elements typically allowed in code applications
calibrationRequirements.tcgDac: TCG (Time Corrected Gain) plot built per code-case requirements

asme: BPVC Sec V Art. 4 Mand. Appx IV
ASME Code Case 2235 (PAUT in lieu of RT)

prerequisiteCertifications: Body of Knowledge per ASNT TC-1A latest
outputArtifacts: Encoded data set with positional record
limitationsAndCaveats: Operator skill gap — PAUT Level II rarer than UT
Setup time longer than conventional UT

TOFD.name: Time-of-Flight Diffraction
TOFD.principle: Pitch-catch transducer pair on opposite sides of weld; defects diffract ultrasonic energy from crack tips; arrival time of diffracted signals precisely sizes through-wall depth; produces D-scan grayscale image with lateral wave + back-wall reference.
typicalUseCases: Weld inspection on heavy-wall pressure vessels and pipe (paired with PAUT)
Fatigue crack monitoring on offshore structures
Code-Case PAUT+TOFD combos for RT replacement

calibrationRequirements.frequency: PCS (Probe Center Spacing) verified per weld thickness; lateral wave + back wall identified at start of each weld
blocks: Weld-specific block w/ side-drilled holes (SDH) at known depths
calibrationRequirements.asmeRef: ASME BPVC Section V Article 4 + Mand. Appx III (TOFD)
calibrationRequirements.deadZones: Surface dead zone (lateral wave) + back-wall dead zone — typically 5-10% of thickness each end

asme: BPVC Sec V Art. 4 Mand. Appx III

limitationsAndCaveats: Not effective for porosity (omnidirectional) — needs PAUT pair

ECT.name: Eddy Current Array (ECA / ECT)
ECT.principle: Multi-element ET probe (8-128 coils) fired in multiplex pattern; produces C-scan image of surface and near-surface flaws in single pass; eliminates raster scanning vs. single-coil ET.
typicalUseCases: Aerospace lap-joint and skin inspection (corrosion + cracks)
Weld toe crack scanning (in lieu of MT on coated parts)
Tank floor scanning under coating (thin floors)
primaryIndustries: Aerospace MRO (737 NG, A320 lap joints)

calibrationRequirements.frequency: Reference notch standard at start of each setup; channel-balance + null check on every probe
calibrationRequirements.asmeRef: ASME BPVC Section V Art. 8 + Mand. Appx

limitationsAndCaveats: Probe geometry must match scan surface

GWT.name: Guided Wave Testing
GWT.principle: Low-frequency (20-100 kHz) torsional/longitudinal guided ultrasonic waves propagate along pipe axis from collar of transducers; reflections from corrosion, cracks, welds, and supports indicate flaw locations up to 50+ m each direction; pipe acts as waveguide.
typicalUseCases: Inaccessible pipe screening (under road crossings, insulated, buried)

instrumentUSD.models: Guided Ultrasonics Wavemaker, Eddyfi Teletest, Olympus QSR1

calibrationRequirements.frequency: DAC built per pipe diameter / wall / coating per scan; weld signal used as cal reference
calibrationRequirements.asmeRef: ASME BPVC Section V Art. 18 (Acoustic Pulse Reflectometry adjacent)

complementaryMethods: UT for follow-up sizing of GWT calls

LT.name: Leak Testing
LT.fullName: Leak Testing (Bubble, Helium Mass Spec, Pressure Decay, Ultrasonic Leak Detection)
LT.principle: Pressure differential creates fluid flow through leak path; detected by bubble formation in soap film, helium tracer gas via mass spectrometer, pressure decay over time, or acoustic emission from leak.
typicalUseCases: Pressure vessel hydrostatic / pneumatic leak qualification

calibrationRequirements.frequency: Helium leak detector cal per shift via calibrated leak; pressure gauges annual

limitationsAndCaveats: Method-specific sensitivity vastly different (bubble ~1e-4 vs helium 1e-10)
Temperature stability critical for pressure decay

AE.name: Acoustic Emission Testing
AE.principle: Active flaws under stress emit transient elastic waves (stress waves); piezo sensors mounted on structure detect bursts; source location triangulated from time-of-arrival differences across sensor array; identifies actively growing defects (not static).
typicalUseCases: Pressure vessel proof-test monitoring (per ASME Sec V Art. 11/12)
Storage tank floor leak detection (LCC scan)
Composite vessel CNG/H2 cylinder qualification (per CARB/PRD)

calibrationRequirements.frequency: Pencil-lead break (Hsu-Nielsen source) at every sensor at start of test per ASTM E976
calibrationRequirements.asmeRef: ASME BPVC Section V Art. 11 (Fiber-Reinforced) / Art. 12 (Metal Vessels) / Art. 13 (Continuous Monitoring)

complementaryMethods: UT/PAUT for follow-up of AE calls
